newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas up on Taiwan tender.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas up on Taiwan tender.

text.p: Singapore gasoline prices edged higher, supported by Taiwan's tender result and talk the market may have bottomed out, traders said on Tuesday.
"There a number of firm bids seen in the last few days, indicating that there may be genuine buyers out there," said one Japanese trader.
A bid was seen for 97-octane cargo for end May loading at $25.10, compared with bids on Monday at $24.95. But there was a lack of offers to close deals, traders said.
Taiwan awarded two cargoes of unleaded reformate at $25.30 per barrel cost-and-freight second-half June, 10 cents above its previous award for early June cargoes.
The award indicated a recent price slide was finding buying support.
Some sources said the market was still weak, with floating bids heard 40-50 cents under Singapore published quotes, free-on-board.
They cited Star refinery's closed tender to export 220,000 barrel of 92-octance gasoline for June 2-6 lifting, which will add pressure to prices.
But one trader said a Dutch trader who had won the June 1-15 Taiwan reformate import tender may be short into that tender and would seek the supplies.
India has also issued a tender to export high aromatic naphtha and liquefied petroleum gas for May 25-27 loading. The tender will close May 16 and will be valid for one day.
Talk was scarce in the naphtha market as Japanese traders back from a long week end were sidelined, looking for fresh factors to determine market direction.
One Japanese trader said an opened arbitrage window will lure more supplies to the east, dampening prices further.
Naphtha swaps were steady at $21.00/$21.20 for May and $21.20/$21.40 for June.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
